exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Cloud-based ingress ACL misconfigurations map directly to cloud firewall modification techniques that expose resources to unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Network Device Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Network device firewall modifications represent the network-layer equivalent of ingress ACL misconfigurations at boundary devices.

exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of egress filtering enables attackers to exfiltrate data over unencrypted protocols without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing egress controls allow data exfiltration over alternative protocols that bypass security monitoring.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Without egress filtering, attackers can freely exfiltrate data to external web services without interception.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: VPN gateways are external remote services whose excessive trust propagation can allow attackers to pivot into internal networks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Over-trusted VPN gateways bridge network security boundaries, enabling lateral movement across zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: VPN trust propagation can be exploited through protocol tunneling to route malicious traffic through trusted VPN connections.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Domain Fronting
exploitedBy.relevance: Domain fronting techniques can exploit load balancer configurations to route traffic to unintended backend zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Devices
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared management planes across boundary devices represent a compromise path where one device's access grants control over others.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Address Translation Traversal
exploitedBy.relevance: Split tunneling gaps allow traffic to bypass NAT and VPN enforcement, directly enabling network boundary traversal.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-hop Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: Without east-west controls, attackers can chain internal hosts as multi-hop proxies to reach deeper network segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Encrypted Channel
exploitedBy.relevance: VPN termination blind spots prevent detection of encrypted channels used for command-and-control or data exfiltration.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Blind spots at VPN termination create opportunities where network sniffing or traffic interception goes unmonitored.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Duplication
exploitedBy.relevance: Asymmetric routing can involve traffic duplication or mirroring that causes packets to traverse inspection points inconsistently.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Credential reuse across zones exploits valid accounts to authenticate to multiple boundary systems with the same stolen credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Credential stuffing directly describes the reuse of credentials across multiple boundary systems and security zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Gathering boundary credentials enables their reuse across multiple zones as part of reconnaissance and lateral movement planning.

exploitedBy.name: Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
exploitedBy.relevance: Stale firewall policies may result from cleared or untracked configuration changes that obscure the true security posture.
